families.name: Kinases
families.description: Enzymes that add phosphate groups to switch other proteins on or off.

families.name: Proteases & regulators
families.description: Cut other proteins (or control the enzymes that do).

families.name: Metabolic enzymes
families.description: Build and break down sugars, fats, nucleotides and other small molecules.

families.name: Chaperones & proteostasis
families.description: Fold, refold, tag and dispose of other proteins.

families.name: Transporters & channels
families.description: Move ions and molecules across membranes.

families.name: Receptors
families.description: Detect a signal (hormone, light, neurotransmitter) and relay it.

families.name: Switches & regulators
families.description: Molecular switches, adaptors and life/death regulators inside signaling networks.

families.name: Transcription factors
families.description: Bind DNA and decide which genes are switched on.

families.name: Genome machinery
families.description: Copy, read, package and repair DNA and RNA.

families.name: Structural & adhesion
families.description: Give cells and tissues their shape, strength and attachments.

families.name: Motors
families.description: Convert chemical energy into movement or rotation.

families.name: Immune & defense
families.description: Recognise and destroy pathogens and abnormal cells.

families.name: Hormones & cytokines
families.description: Secreted messengers that signal between cells and organs.

families.name: Carriers & storage
families.description: Bind and carry oxygen, iron, electrons, fats and other cargo.

locations.name: Nucleus
locations.description: Inside the nucleus, near the DNA.

locations.name: Cytosol
locations.description: The fluid interior of the cell.

locations.name: Cytoskeleton
locations.description: On the internal scaffolding of filaments and tubules.

locations.name: ER, Golgi & vesicles
locations.description: In the endomembrane system: ER, Golgi, lysosomes, peroxisomes and vesicles.

locations.name: Plasma membrane
locations.description: In or on the cell's outer membrane.

locations.name: Extracellular
locations.description: Secreted outside the cell: blood, tissue fluid, extracellular matrix.

pathways.name: Glycolysis
pathways.description: Breaking glucose down to pyruvate for quick energy.

pathways.name: Insulin & glucose control
pathways.description: How insulin and glucagon keep blood sugar in range.

pathways.name: EGFR → RAS → MAPK growth signaling
pathways.description: The growth-factor relay most often hijacked in cancer.

pathways.name: Cell cycle
pathways.description: Checkpoints and engines that drive a cell to divide.

pathways.name: DNA damage response
pathways.description: Sensing broken DNA, pausing the cell and repairing it.

pathways.name: Apoptosis
pathways.description: Programmed cell death: the orderly self-destruct sequence.

pathways.name: Mitochondrial energy (TCA & OXPHOS)
pathways.description: Burning fuel in mitochondria to make most of the cell's ATP.

pathways.name: Protein quality control
pathways.description: Folding, refolding and destroying proteins; failure leads to aggregation.

pathways.name: Blood clotting
pathways.description: The protease cascade that turns liquid blood into a clot.

pathways.name: Muscle contraction
pathways.description: Calcium-triggered sliding of myosin along actin.

pathways.name: Innate immunity & inflammation
pathways.description: The fast, built-in defense against infection.

pathways.name: Adaptive immunity
pathways.description: Antibodies and T cells that learn and remember.

pathways.name: Alzheimer's disease
pathways.description: Proteins at the centre of the amyloid and tau story.

pathways.name: Oxygen transport & sensing
pathways.description: Carrying oxygen and responding when it runs low.

proteins.name: Hemoglobin subunit alpha
proteins.milestone: Hemoglobin crystals observed (Hünefeld)
proteins.blurb: The α half of adult hemoglobin (α₂β₂).

proteins.name: Hemoglobin subunit beta
proteins.milestone: Hemoglobin crystals observed (Hünefeld)
proteins.blurb: Carries oxygen in red blood cells (with α chains).

proteins.name: Immunoglobulin κ constant
proteins.milestone: Free light chains in urine described (Bence Jones)
proteins.blurb: Constant region of antibody κ light chains.

misfolded.name: Immunoglobulin light-chain amyloid
misfolded.description: Abnormal plasma cells overproduce one light chain (more often λ than κ), which misfolds into amyloid. The most common systemic amyloidosis. The structure shown is a λ fibril.

proteins.name: Myosin-7 (β-cardiac myosin)
proteins.milestone: Myosin extracted from muscle (Kühne)
proteins.blurb: Walks along actin using ATP, powering every heartbeat.

proteins.name: Prothrombin (thrombin)
proteins.milestone: Thrombin proposed as the clotting ferment (Schmidt)
proteins.blurb: Central clotting protease; converts fibrinogen into fibrin.

proteins.name: Trypsin-1
proteins.milestone: Trypsin named (Kühne)
proteins.blurb: Digestive protease from the pancreas; cuts after lysine and arginine.

proteins.name: Rhodopsin
proteins.milestone: 'Visual purple' described in the retina (Boll)
proteins.blurb: Light-sensing receptor of rod cells: the first step of night vision.

proteins.name: Histone H3.1
proteins.milestone: Histones discovered (Kossel)
proteins.blurb: Spool protein that DNA wraps around; its tail modifications form the 'histone code'.

proteins.name: Immunoglobulin heavy constant γ1
proteins.milestone: Antitoxin activity of serum discovered (von Behring & Kitasato)
proteins.blurb: Constant region of IgG antibodies; recruits immune cells and complement.

proteins.name: Serum albumin
proteins.milestone: Serum albumin crystallised (Gürber)
proteins.blurb: Most abundant blood protein: holds water in vessels and carries fats and drugs.

proteins.name: Catalase
proteins.milestone: Catalase named (Loew)
proteins.blurb: Peroxisome enzyme that splits hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen.

proteins.name: Insulin
proteins.milestone: Discovered (Banting & Best); first protein sequenced (Sanger, 1955)
proteins.blurb: Lowers blood sugar by telling cells to take up glucose.

misfolded.name: Insulin amyloid
misfolded.description: Repeated injection at the same site can make insulin form amyloid lumps that block its absorption.

proteins.name: Lysozyme C
proteins.milestone: Discovered in nasal mucus (Fleming)
proteins.blurb: Antibacterial enzyme in tears and saliva that cuts bacterial cell walls.

misfolded.name: Lysozyme amyloid
misfolded.description: Destabilising mutations let lysozyme partly unfold and form amyloid in the kidney, liver and gut.

proteins.name: Glucagon
proteins.milestone: Glucagon discovered as a pancreatic factor that raises blood sugar (Kimball & Murlin)
proteins.blurb: Raises blood sugar between meals: insulin's opposite.

proteins.name: Cytochrome c
proteins.milestone: Cytochromes rediscovered and named (Keilin)
proteins.blurb: Shuttles electrons in respiration; released from mitochondria it triggers apoptosis.

proteins.name: Hexokinase-1
proteins.milestone: Hexokinase activity described (Meyerhof)
proteins.blurb: Traps glucose inside the cell by adding a phosphate: glycolysis step 1.

proteins.name: Amine oxidase [flavin-containing] B
proteins.milestone: Tyramine oxidase (later monoamine oxidase) described (Hare)
proteins.blurb: Breaks down dopamine on the mitochondrial outer membrane.

proteins.name: Glucose-6-phosphate 1-dehydrogenase
proteins.milestone: Discovered by Warburg & Christian
proteins.blurb: Makes NADPH that protects red blood cells from oxidative damage.

proteins.name: Acetylcholinesterase
proteins.milestone: Cholinesterase named (Stedman et al.)
proteins.blurb: Clears acetylcholine from the synapse in milliseconds; the target of nerve agents.

proteins.name: Carbonic anhydrase 2
proteins.milestone: Carbonic anhydrase discovered in red cells (Meldrum & Roughton)
proteins.blurb: One of the fastest enzymes known: interconverts CO₂ and bicarbonate.

proteins.name: Pyruvate kinase PKM
proteins.milestone: Pyruvate kinase reaction described (Lohmann & Meyerhof)
proteins.blurb: Final step of glycolysis; its M2 form helps tumours divert sugar into growth.

proteins.name: Coagulation factor VIII
proteins.milestone: Antihemophilic globulin described (Patek & Taylor)
proteins.blurb: Cofactor for factor IX; missing in hemophilia A.

proteins.name: Ferritin heavy chain
proteins.milestone: Ferritin isolated from spleen (Laufberger)
proteins.blurb: Hollow cage that stores up to 4,500 iron atoms safely.

proteins.name: Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase
proteins.milestone: Isolated and characterised by Warburg & Christian
proteins.blurb: Glycolysis step 6; so abundant it is the lab's go-to loading control.

proteins.name: Actin, alpha skeletal muscle
proteins.milestone: Actin discovered in muscle (Straub)
proteins.blurb: Forms the thin filaments myosin pulls on; one of the most abundant proteins.

proteins.name: Transthyretin
proteins.milestone: Identified as 'prealbumin' in blood (Kabat et al.)
proteins.blurb: Carries thyroid hormone and vitamin A in blood and spinal fluid.

misfolded.name: Transthyretin amyloid
misfolded.description: The four-part TTR complex falls apart and the pieces misfold into amyloid in nerves and heart. Tafamidis works by holding the complex together.

proteins.name: Coagulation factor V
proteins.milestone: Discovered by Owren in a patient with a bleeding disorder
proteins.blurb: Cofactor that speeds up factor X about 300,000-fold.

proteins.name: Serotransferrin
proteins.milestone: Iron-binding blood protein identified (Schade & Caroline)
proteins.blurb: Carries iron in the blood and delivers it via the transferrin receptor.

proteins.name: Citrate synthase
proteins.milestone: Condensing enzyme of the citric acid cycle isolated (Stern & Ochoa)
proteins.blurb: First step of the Krebs cycle inside mitochondria.

proteins.name: Phenylalanine-4-hydroxylase
proteins.milestone: Phenylketonuria shown to be a PAH deficiency (Jervis)
proteins.blurb: Turns phenylalanine into tyrosine in the liver.

proteins.name: Collagen alpha-1(I) chain
proteins.milestone: Triple-helix structure proposed (Ramachandran & Kartha)
proteins.blurb: Most abundant protein in the body: the cable of bone, skin and tendon.

proteins.name: Angiotensin-converting enzyme
proteins.milestone: Discovered as the enzyme converting angiotensin I to II (Skeggs)
proteins.blurb: Makes the blood-pressure-raising hormone angiotensin II.

proteins.name: Coagulation factor X
proteins.milestone: Identified as Stuart–Prower factor
proteins.blurb: Converts prothrombin into thrombin; where both clotting branches meet.

proteins.name: Somatotropin (growth hormone)
proteins.milestone: Human growth hormone isolated (Li & Papkoff)
proteins.blurb: Pituitary hormone driving growth in childhood.

proteins.name: Sodium/potassium-transporting ATPase α1
proteins.milestone: Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase discovered (Skou, Nobel 1997)
proteins.blurb: Pumps 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in; uses about a fifth of your energy at rest.

proteins.name: Dihydrofolate reductase
proteins.milestone: Folate-reducing enzyme characterised as the target of antifolates
proteins.blurb: Recycles folate needed to build DNA; blocked by methotrexate.

proteins.name: HLA class I histocompatibility antigen, A alpha chain
proteins.milestone: First human leukocyte antigen described (Dausset, Nobel 1980)
proteins.blurb: Shows protein fragments from inside the cell to killer T cells.

proteins.name: Myoglobin
proteins.milestone: First protein 3D structure solved (Kendrew, Nobel 1962)
proteins.blurb: Stores oxygen in muscle; gives red meat its colour.

proteins.name: 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA reductase
proteins.milestone: Identified as the rate-limiting step of cholesterol synthesis
proteins.blurb: ER enzyme controlling cholesterol production; the target of statins.

proteins.name: ATP synthase subunit β, mitochondrial
proteins.milestone: F1-ATPase isolated (Racker et al.)
proteins.blurb: Rotary motor that spins about 100 times a second to make ATP.

proteins.name: SERCA2 calcium pump
proteins.milestone: Sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium pump described (Hasselbach & Makinose)
proteins.blurb: Pumps calcium back into the ER so muscle can relax.

proteins.name: Pro-epidermal growth factor
proteins.milestone: Discovered by Cohen (Nobel 1986)
proteins.blurb: Growth factor that activates EGFR to stimulate cell division.

proteins.name: Estrogen receptor α
proteins.milestone: Estrogen-binding receptor demonstrated (Jensen & Jacobson)
proteins.blurb: Hormone-activated transcription factor driving most breast cancers.

proteins.name: Protein disulfide-isomerase
proteins.milestone: Enzyme that reshuffles disulfide bonds discovered (Anfinsen lab)
proteins.blurb: Forms and fixes disulfide bonds in newly made secreted proteins.

proteins.name: Poly [ADP-ribose] polymerase 1
proteins.milestone: Poly(ADP-ribose) discovered (Chambon et al.)
proteins.blurb: Detects single-strand DNA breaks and recruits repair proteins.

proteins.name: Alpha-1-antitrypsin
proteins.milestone: Deficiency discovered in patients with emphysema (Laurell & Eriksson)
proteins.blurb: Protease inhibitor that protects the lungs from neutrophil elastase.

misfolded.name: Z alpha-1-antitrypsin polymers
misfolded.description: The Z variant opens up and links into long chains (polymers) that clog the ER of liver cells, while too little reaches the lungs. A 'serpinopathy': misfolding without amyloid.

proteins.name: Cytoplasmic dynein 1 heavy chain 1
proteins.milestone: Dynein discovered in cilia (Gibbons)
proteins.blurb: Carries cargo inwards along microtubules toward the cell centre.

proteins.name: Interferon gamma
proteins.milestone: Described as a virus inhibitor made by stimulated leukocytes (Wheelock)
proteins.blurb: Activates macrophages and coordinates T-cell immunity.

proteins.name: Beta-2-microglobulin
proteins.milestone: Isolated from urine (Berggård & Bearn)
proteins.blurb: Small partner that stabilises every MHC class I molecule.

misfolded.name: β2-microglobulin amyloid
misfolded.description: Builds up when kidneys fail and forms amyloid in joints and bones.

proteins.name: cAMP-dependent protein kinase catalytic subunit α
proteins.milestone: cAMP-dependent protein kinase discovered (Walsh, Perkins & Krebs)
proteins.blurb: Reads cAMP levels and phosphorylates targets after hormones like adrenaline bind.

proteins.name: Tubulin beta chain
proteins.milestone: Tubulin named as the protein of microtubules (Mohri)
proteins.blurb: Builds microtubules: the cell's tracks and the mitotic spindle.

proteins.name: Androgen receptor
proteins.milestone: Androgen-binding receptor protein characterised
proteins.blurb: Testosterone-activated transcription factor; drives prostate cancer.

proteins.name: DNA-directed RNA polymerase II subunit RPB1
proteins.milestone: Separate eukaryotic RNA polymerases discovered (Roeder & Rutter)
proteins.blurb: Transcribes all protein-coding genes into messenger RNA.

proteins.name: Superoxide dismutase [Cu-Zn]
proteins.milestone: Superoxide dismutase activity discovered (McCord & Fridovich)
proteins.blurb: Destroys toxic superoxide radicals; mutations cause inherited ALS.

misfolded.name: Misfolded SOD1 aggregates
misfolded.description: Mutant SOD1 loses its metal ions, unfolds and forms aggregates that can seed misfolding in neighbouring motor neurons.

proteins.name: Calmodulin-1
proteins.milestone: Calcium-dependent activator discovered (Cheung)
proteins.blurb: Universal calcium sensor that switches dozens of enzymes on.

proteins.name: Acetylcholine receptor subunit α (muscle)
proteins.milestone: Acetylcholine receptor isolated using snake venom toxins (Changeux)
proteins.blurb: Ion channel at the nerve–muscle junction that triggers contraction.

proteins.name: DNA polymerase γ catalytic subunit
proteins.milestone: Mitochondrial DNA polymerase activity described
proteins.blurb: The only polymerase that copies mitochondrial DNA.

proteins.name: Insulin receptor
proteins.milestone: Insulin binding to cell-surface receptors measured (Cuatrecasas)
proteins.blurb: Tyrosine kinase receptor that hands the insulin signal to IRS1.

proteins.name: Serum amyloid A-1 protein
proteins.milestone: Identified as the blood precursor of AA amyloid
proteins.blurb: Acute-phase protein that shoots up during inflammation and carries lipids.

misfolded.name: Serum amyloid A (AA) amyloid
diseases: AA amyloidosis (chronic inflammation, e.g. rheumatoid arthritis)
misfolded.description: Long-lasting inflammation keeps SAA high; fragments form amyloid, mainly in the kidneys.

proteins.name: Apolipoprotein E
proteins.milestone: Arginine-rich apolipoprotein described (Shore & Shore)
proteins.blurb: Carries cholesterol in blood and brain; ε4 is the strongest genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer's.

proteins.name: Fibronectin
proteins.milestone: Cell-surface 'LETS' protein described (Hynes)
proteins.blurb: Matrix glue that cells grip via integrins during wound healing.

proteins.name: Mu-type opioid receptor
proteins.milestone: Opioid receptors demonstrated (Pert & Snyder)
proteins.blurb: Receptor for endorphins, morphine and fentanyl.

proteins.name: Calreticulin
proteins.milestone: High-affinity calcium-binding protein of muscle ER described (MacLennan)
proteins.blurb: ER calcium store and glycoprotein chaperone.

proteins.name: Heat shock 70 kDa protein 1A (Hsp70)
proteins.milestone: Heat-shock proteins identified (Tissières, Mitchell & Tracy)
proteins.blurb: Grabs exposed sticky patches on unfolded proteins and helps them refold.

proteins.name: Low-density lipoprotein receptor
proteins.milestone: Discovered by Brown & Goldstein (Nobel 1985)
proteins.blurb: Pulls LDL ('bad cholesterol') out of the blood.

proteins.name: Clathrin heavy chain 1
proteins.milestone: Clathrin named as the coat protein of vesicles (Pearse)
proteins.blurb: Three-legged triskelion that builds cages around budding vesicles.

proteins.name: Microtubule-associated protein tau
proteins.milestone: Isolated as a microtubule-assembly factor (Weingarten et al.)
proteins.blurb: Stabilises microtubules in neuron axons.

misfolded.name: Tau filaments (tangles)
misfolded.description: Over-phosphorylated tau detaches from microtubules and folds into disease-specific filaments that form neurofibrillary tangles.

proteins.name: Tumour necrosis factor
proteins.milestone: Serum factor causing tumour necrosis described (Carswell et al.)
proteins.blurb: Master inflammatory cytokine; target of blockbuster anti-inflammatory drugs.

proteins.name: Ubiquitin
proteins.milestone: Ubiquitin isolated (Goldstein et al.)
proteins.blurb: Small tag chained onto proteins to mark them for destruction or new jobs.

proteins.name: ATP-dependent translocase ABCB1 (P-glycoprotein)
proteins.milestone: Discovered in drug-resistant cancer cells (Juliano & Ling)
proteins.blurb: Pumps drugs out of cells; a major cause of chemotherapy resistance.

proteins.name: DNA polymerase δ catalytic subunit
proteins.milestone: DNA polymerase δ identified (Byrnes et al.)
proteins.blurb: Copies the lagging strand during DNA replication with built-in proofreading.

proteins.name: Prostaglandin G/H synthase 1 (COX-1)
proteins.milestone: Cyclooxygenase purified (Hemler & Lands; Miyamoto et al.)
proteins.blurb: Makes prostaglandins that protect the stomach and help platelets clot.

proteins.name: Voltage-dependent anion-selective channel 1
proteins.milestone: Mitochondrial anion channel discovered (Schein, Colombini & Finkelstein)
proteins.blurb: Main pore in the mitochondrial outer membrane; lets ATP and metabolites through.

proteins.name: Cadherin-1 (E-cadherin)
proteins.milestone: Calcium-dependent cell adhesion described (Takeichi)
proteins.blurb: Zips neighbouring epithelial cells together; lost when cancers spread.

proteins.name: Erythropoietin
proteins.milestone: Purified from urine (Miyake, Kung & Goldwasser)
proteins.blurb: Kidney hormone telling the bone marrow to make red blood cells.

proteins.name: Titin
proteins.milestone: Giant elastic muscle protein discovered (Maruyama: 'connectin')
proteins.blurb: The largest known human protein: a molecular spring spanning half a sarcomere.

proteins.name: Epidermal growth factor receptor
proteins.milestone: EGF receptor identified (Carpenter & Cohen)
proteins.blurb: Receptor tyrosine kinase that starts the RAS→MAPK growth relay.

proteins.name: Prelamin-A/C
proteins.milestone: Nuclear lamina proteins identified (Gerace, Blum & Blobel)
proteins.blurb: Meshwork lining the inside of the nucleus, giving it shape.

proteins.name: Vimentin
proteins.milestone: Intermediate filament protein of mesenchymal cells named (Franke et al.)
proteins.blurb: Intermediate filament that cushions cells against mechanical stress.

proteins.name: D(2) dopamine receptor
proteins.milestone: D1/D2 dopamine receptor classes proposed (Kebabian & Calne)
proteins.blurb: Dopamine receptor targeted by antipsychotics and Parkinson's drugs.

proteins.name: Cellular tumour antigen p53
proteins.milestone: Discovered bound to SV40 large T antigen (Lane & Crawford; Levine; Old)
proteins.blurb: 'Guardian of the genome': halts division or orders apoptosis after DNA damage. Mutated in about half of all cancers.

proteins.name: Guanine nucleotide-binding protein G(s) α
proteins.milestone: Gs protein purified (Gilman, Nobel 1994)
proteins.blurb: Couples receptors like β2-adrenergic to cAMP production.

proteins.name: B-lymphocyte antigen CD20
proteins.milestone: B1 antigen identified on B cells (Stashenko et al.)
proteins.blurb: B-cell surface marker; a target for wiping out B cells.

proteins.name: DNA topoisomerase 2-α
proteins.milestone: Eukaryotic type II topoisomerase characterised
proteins.blurb: Cuts and rejoins both DNA strands to untangle chromosomes.

proteins.name: Tyrosine-protein kinase ABL1
proteins.milestone: Human c-ABL identified as counterpart of the Abelson leukemia virus oncogene
proteins.blurb: Fused to BCR in chronic myeloid leukemia; the target that launched targeted cancer drugs.

proteins.name: Heat shock protein HSP 90-alpha
proteins.milestone: HSP90 characterised as an abundant cytosolic chaperone
proteins.blurb: Late-stage chaperone that keeps kinases and hormone receptors ready to act.

proteins.name: GTPase KRas
proteins.milestone: Mutant RAS found in human cancer cells
proteins.blurb: On/off GTP switch under the membrane; the most frequently mutated cancer gene.

proteins.name: Myc proto-oncogene protein
proteins.milestone: Human c-MYC identified as counterpart of a viral oncogene
proteins.blurb: Master growth transcription factor; overactive in most cancers.

proteins.name: Major prion protein (PrPᶜ)
proteins.milestone: Prion protein identified (Prusiner, Nobel 1997)
proteins.blurb: Normal cell-surface protein of neurons, attached by a lipid anchor; function still debated.

misfolded.name: Scrapie prion protein (PrPˢᶜ)
diseases: Scrapie, BSE ('mad cow'), chronic wasting disease (animals)
misfolded.description: The only true infectious protein: PrPˢᶜ converts normal PrPᶜ into more PrPˢᶜ and can transmit disease between individuals, and even species.

proteins.name: G2/mitotic-specific cyclin-B1
proteins.milestone: Cyclins discovered in sea urchin eggs (Hunt, Nobel 2001)
proteins.blurb: Rises and crashes every cycle, switching CDK1 on for mitosis.

proteins.name: Clusterin
proteins.milestone: Isolated from ram rete testis fluid
proteins.blurb: Extracellular chaperone that mops up misfolded proteins; a genetic Alzheimer's risk factor.

proteins.name: Endoplasmic reticulum chaperone BiP
proteins.milestone: Immunoglobulin heavy-chain binding protein identified (Haas & Wabl)
proteins.blurb: Main ER chaperone and the sensor that triggers the unfolded protein response.

proteins.name: Apoptosis regulator Bcl-2
proteins.milestone: Discovered at the t(14;18) translocation in follicular lymphoma
proteins.blurb: Guards mitochondria against BAX; overproduced cancer cells refuse to die.

proteins.name: Receptor tyrosine-protein kinase erbB-2 (HER2)
proteins.milestone: neu oncogene identified in rat tumours (Weinberg lab)
proteins.blurb: EGFR relative overproduced in about 1 in 5 breast cancers.

proteins.name: Neutrophil defensin 1
proteins.milestone: Human neutrophil defensins described (Ganz, Lehrer et al.)
proteins.blurb: Short antimicrobial peptide that punctures microbial membranes.

proteins.name: Kinesin-1 heavy chain
proteins.milestone: Kinesin discovered in squid axons (Vale, Reese & Sheetz)
proteins.blurb: Two-legged walker carrying cargo outwards along microtubules.

proteins.name: Glucocorticoid receptor
proteins.milestone: Cloned (Hollenberg, Evans et al.)
proteins.blurb: Cortisol receptor; waits in the cytosol, then enters the nucleus to calm inflammation.

proteins.name: Perforin-1
proteins.milestone: Pore-forming protein of killer lymphocytes purified (Podack; Young)
proteins.blurb: Stored in killer-cell granules; punches holes in infected and cancer cells.

proteins.name: Solute carrier family 2, member 1 (GLUT1)
proteins.milestone: Glucose transporter cloned (Mueckler et al.)
proteins.blurb: Constant glucose supply for red cells and the brain.

proteins.name: Telomerase reverse transcriptase
proteins.milestone: Telomerase discovered (Greider & Blackburn, Nobel 2009); human TERT cloned in 1997
proteins.blurb: Rebuilds chromosome ends; switched back on in most cancers.

proteins.name: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor
proteins.milestone: Cloned; the first hormone GPCR sequence (Lefkowitz & Kobilka)
proteins.blurb: Adrenaline receptor that relaxes the airways.

proteins.name: Fibrillin-1
proteins.milestone: Identified as the main component of microfibrils (Sakai et al.)
proteins.blurb: Builds elastic microfibrils and controls TGF-β signalling.

proteins.name: Interleukin-6
proteins.milestone: Cloned as B-cell stimulatory factor 2 (Hirano, Kishimoto et al.)
proteins.blurb: Cytokine driving fever and acute-phase proteins.

proteins.name: Integrin beta-1
proteins.milestone: 'Integrin' named (Hynes et al.)
proteins.blurb: Anchors cells to the extracellular matrix and senses its stiffness.

proteins.name: Retinoblastoma-associated protein
proteins.milestone: First tumour-suppressor gene cloned
proteins.blurb: Brake on the cell cycle; holds E2F until CDK4/6 phosphorylates it.

proteins.name: Transcription factor p65 (NF-κB RelA)
proteins.milestone: NF-κB discovered (Sen & Baltimore)
proteins.blurb: Held in the cytosol until danger signals release it to switch on inflammation genes.

proteins.name: Amyloid-beta precursor protein
proteins.milestone: Gene cloned; amyloid-β peptide sequenced in 1984 (Glenner & Wong)
proteins.blurb: Membrane protein whose cleavage releases amyloid-β, the core of Alzheimer's plaques.

misfolded.name: Amyloid-β fibrils and plaques
misfolded.description: Amyloid-β (40–42 amino acids cut from APP) stacks into β-sheet fibrils that form plaques and can seed further aggregation.

proteins.name: Cyclin-dependent kinase 1
proteins.milestone: Human CDC2 found to rescue yeast cell-cycle mutants (Lee & Nurse)
proteins.blurb: The master engine of cell division; partners with cyclin B to trigger mitosis.

proteins.name: Cytotoxic T-lymphocyte protein 4
proteins.milestone: Cloned from cytotoxic T cells (Brunet et al.; Allison, Nobel 2018)
proteins.blurb: Early checkpoint brake on T-cell activation.

proteins.name: Dystrophin
proteins.milestone: Gene and protein identified (Kunkel; Hoffman)
proteins.blurb: Links the inner cytoskeleton to the membrane, protecting muscle fibres.

proteins.name: Islet amyloid polypeptide (amylin)
proteins.milestone: Isolated from amyloid in diabetic pancreas (Cooper; Westermark)
proteins.blurb: Released alongside insulin; slows stomach emptying.

misfolded.name: Islet amyloid
misfolded.description: Found in the pancreatic islets of most people with type 2 diabetes, where it is toxic to insulin-producing β cells.

proteins.name: Serine/threonine-protein kinase B-raf
proteins.milestone: Human B-RAF cloned
proteins.blurb: RAF kinase directly downstream of RAS; mutated in about half of melanomas.

proteins.name: DNA (cytosine-5)-methyltransferase 1
proteins.milestone: Mammalian DNA methyltransferase cloned (Bestor et al.)
proteins.blurb: Copies DNA methylation marks onto new DNA, preserving epigenetic memory.

proteins.name: 60 kDa heat shock protein, mitochondrial
proteins.milestone: Shown to be required for folding imported mitochondrial proteins
proteins.blurb: Barrel-shaped folding chamber inside mitochondria.

proteins.name: Proteasome subunit β5
proteins.milestone: The 'proteasome' named as the cell's multicatalytic protease
proteins.blurb: Main cutting site of the proteasome, the shredder for ubiquitin-tagged proteins.

proteins.name: Alpha-synuclein
proteins.milestone: Identified in synaptic vesicles of the electric ray (Maroteaux et al.)
proteins.blurb: Regulates neurotransmitter vesicle release at synapses.

misfolded.name: α-Synuclein fibrils (Lewy bodies)
misfolded.description: Unfolded α-synuclein stacks into fibrils that build Lewy bodies and spread between connected neurons.

proteins.name: TATA-box-binding protein
proteins.milestone: TATA-binding factor TFIID characterised
proteins.blurb: Bends DNA at promoters to position RNA polymerase II.

proteins.name: Transcription factor A, mitochondrial
proteins.milestone: Mitochondrial transcription factor A characterised
proteins.blurb: Packages mitochondrial DNA and starts its transcription.

proteins.name: Voltage-dependent L-type calcium channel α1C
proteins.milestone: Cardiac L-type calcium channel cloned
proteins.blurb: Lets calcium in to trigger heart and smooth-muscle contraction.

proteins.name: Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator
proteins.milestone: Gene identified as the cause of cystic fibrosis
proteins.blurb: Chloride channel that keeps mucus thin; defective in cystic fibrosis.

proteins.name: Catenin beta-1 (β-catenin)
proteins.milestone: Catenins identified binding E-cadherin (Ozawa, Baribault & Kemler)
proteins.blurb: Links cadherins to actin; also a Wnt-activated transcription co-factor.

proteins.name: Dynamin-1
proteins.milestone: Microtubule-binding GTPase purified (Shpetner & Vallee)
proteins.blurb: Mechanical GTPase that coils around vesicle necks and pinches them off.

proteins.name: Inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor type 1
proteins.milestone: IP₃ receptor cloned (Furuichi et al.)
proteins.blurb: ER calcium-release channel opened by the messenger IP₃.

proteins.name: Solute carrier family 2, member 4 (GLUT4)
proteins.milestone: Insulin-responsive glucose transporter cloned
proteins.blurb: Waits in vesicles until insulin sends it to the membrane to pull in glucose.

proteins.name: Mitochondrial import receptor subunit TOM20
proteins.milestone: Identified in fungal mitochondria as an import receptor
proteins.blurb: Recognises the 'address label' on proteins headed into mitochondria.

proteins.name: Vascular endothelial growth factor A
proteins.milestone: Purified and cloned (Ferrara & Henzel; Leung et al.)
proteins.blurb: Calls new blood vessels to grow; hijacked by tumours and in wet AMD.

proteins.name: Furin
proteins.milestone: Identified as the Golgi pro-protein convertase
proteins.blurb: Golgi protease that activates hormones and receptors; hijacked by many viruses.

proteins.name: Mitogen-activated protein kinase 1 (ERK2)
proteins.milestone: ERK kinases cloned (Boulton et al.)
proteins.blurb: Last kinase of the RAS→RAF→MEK→ERK relay; enters the nucleus to drive growth genes.

proteins.name: POU domain, class 5, transcription factor 1 (OCT4)
proteins.milestone: Identified in embryonic cells; a Yamanaka reprogramming factor in 2006
proteins.blurb: Keeps stem cells pluripotent; one of four factors that reprogram adult cells.

proteins.name: RAC-alpha serine/threonine-protein kinase (AKT1)
proteins.milestone: Human AKT cloned as the cellular counterpart of a viral oncogene
proteins.blurb: Survival and growth kinase; carries the insulin signal to glucose uptake.

proteins.name: Calnexin
proteins.milestone: Identified as an ER membrane chaperone
proteins.blurb: Checks the sugar tags on new glycoproteins and holds them until folded.

proteins.name: Insulin receptor substrate 1
proteins.milestone: Cloned as the main substrate of the insulin receptor (White lab)
proteins.blurb: Docking hub that relays the insulin signal to PI3K and AKT.

proteins.name: Tyrosine-protein kinase JAK2
proteins.milestone: JAK kinases cloned ('just another kinase')
proteins.blurb: Bound to cytokine receptors; switches on STAT transcription factors.

proteins.name: Prostaglandin G/H synthase 2 (COX-2)
proteins.milestone: Inducible cyclooxygenase discovered
proteins.blurb: Inflammation-induced enzyme making pain and fever prostaglandins.

proteins.name: Sodium-dependent serotonin transporter
proteins.milestone: Serotonin transporter cloned
proteins.blurb: Recaptures serotonin after release; blocked by most antidepressants.

proteins.name: Aquaporin-1
proteins.milestone: Identified as the first water channel (Agre, Nobel 2003)
proteins.blurb: Lets water molecules, and only water, flow rapidly across membranes.

proteins.name: Cyclin-dependent kinase 4
proteins.milestone: Identified as the partner kinase of D-type cyclins
proteins.blurb: Pushes cells out of rest (G1) by phosphorylating the brake protein Rb.

proteins.name: Glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor
proteins.milestone: GLP-1 receptor cloned (Thorens)
proteins.blurb: Boosts insulin release after meals and reduces appetite.

proteins.name: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase Mdm2
proteins.milestone: Shown to bind and inhibit p53 (Momand et al.)
proteins.blurb: Tags p53 with ubiquitin for destruction, keeping it low in healthy cells.

proteins.name: Programmed cell death protein 1
proteins.milestone: Cloned (Honjo lab; Nobel 2018)
proteins.blurb: Brake on T cells; tumours exploit it to switch off immune attack.

proteins.name: Sodium channel protein type 5 subunit α (Nav1.5)
proteins.milestone: Cardiac sodium channel cloned
proteins.blurb: Starts every heartbeat's electrical upstroke.

proteins.name: Apoptosis regulator BAX
proteins.milestone: Identified as a BCL-2 binding partner that promotes death (Oltvai, Milliman & Korsmeyer)
proteins.blurb: On a death signal, moves to mitochondria and punches holes in them.

proteins.name: Tyrosine-protein kinase BTK
proteins.milestone: Identified as the gene defective in X-linked agammaglobulinemia
proteins.blurb: Essential for B-cell receptor signaling and B-cell development.

proteins.name: Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1 (p21)
proteins.milestone: Identified as a p53-induced CDK inhibitor
proteins.blurb: Made on p53's orders to halt the cell cycle after DNA damage.

proteins.name: Huntingtin
proteins.milestone: Gene identified as the cause of Huntington's disease
proteins.blurb: Large scaffold protein involved in vesicle transport.

misfolded.name: Polyglutamine-expanded huntingtin aggregates
misfolded.description: Fragments with an expanded glutamine (Q) tract form β-sheet aggregates and nuclear inclusions in neurons.

proteins.name: Lon protease, mitochondrial
proteins.milestone: Human mitochondrial Lon protease cloned
proteins.blurb: Mitochondria's own quality-control protease; degrades damaged matrix proteins.

proteins.name: Sterol regulatory element-binding protein 2
proteins.milestone: Cloned by Brown & Goldstein's lab
proteins.blurb: Parked in the ER membrane; released when cholesterol is low to switch on its synthesis.

proteins.name: Breast cancer type 1 susceptibility protein
proteins.milestone: Gene cloned (Miki et al.)
proteins.blurb: Repairs DNA double-strand breaks by homologous recombination.

proteins.name: Caspase-3
proteins.milestone: CPP32 cloned as a mammalian cell-death protease
proteins.blurb: Executioner protease of apoptosis; cuts hundreds of proteins to dismantle the cell.

proteins.name: Potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily H member 2 (hERG)
proteins.milestone: Linked to inherited long QT syndrome
proteins.blurb: Resets each heartbeat; many drugs fail safety tests by blocking it by accident.

proteins.name: Leptin
proteins.milestone: Cloned from the obese (ob) mouse (Friedman lab)
proteins.blurb: Satiety hormone from fat that tells the brain energy stores are full.

proteins.name: Serine/threonine-protein kinase mTOR
proteins.milestone: Identified as the mammalian target of rapamycin
proteins.blurb: Nutrient sensor on the lysosome surface that decides whether the cell grows.

proteins.name: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ
proteins.milestone: Identified as the master regulator of fat-cell formation
proteins.blurb: Turns on fat-storage genes; boosted by diabetes drugs.

proteins.name: Sodium/glucose cotransporter 2
proteins.milestone: Kidney low-affinity sodium-glucose transporter cloned
proteins.blurb: Reclaims glucose from urine in the kidney.

proteins.name: Signal transducer and activator of transcription 3
proteins.milestone: Identified as an IL-6-activated transcription factor
proteins.blurb: Carries cytokine signals from JAK kinases to the nucleus.

proteins.name: Serine-protein kinase ATM
proteins.milestone: Gene cloned as the cause of ataxia-telangiectasia
proteins.blurb: First responder to DNA double-strand breaks; activates p53 and repair.

proteins.name: Breast cancer type 2 susceptibility protein
proteins.milestone: Gene cloned (Wooster et al.)
proteins.blurb: Loads RAD51 onto broken DNA for repair.

proteins.name: Hypoxia-inducible factor 1-α
proteins.milestone: Purified and cloned (Wang & Semenza; Nobel 2019)
proteins.blurb: Destroyed when oxygen is plentiful; when it runs low, it switches on EPO and blood-vessel genes.

proteins.name: Importin subunit beta-1
proteins.milestone: Identified as the nuclear import receptor
proteins.blurb: Carries proteins through nuclear pores into the nucleus.

proteins.name: Presenilin-1
proteins.milestone: Gene identified in early-onset familial Alzheimer's disease
proteins.blurb: Catalytic core of γ-secretase, which makes the final cut releasing amyloid-β.

proteins.name: TAR DNA-binding protein 43
proteins.milestone: Cloned as a protein binding HIV TAR DNA; linked to ALS and FTD in 2006
proteins.blurb: RNA-binding protein that controls splicing of thousands of genes.

misfolded.name: TDP-43 inclusions
misfolded.description: TDP-43 leaves the nucleus and forms phosphorylated aggregates in the cytosol, losing its normal job while the aggregates spread.

proteins.name: Histone deacetylase 1
proteins.milestone: First histone deacetylase cloned (Taunton, Hassig & Schreiber)
proteins.blurb: Removes acetyl marks from histones, tightening chromatin and silencing genes.

proteins.name: Phosphatase and tensin homolog
proteins.milestone: Identified as a tumour suppressor on chromosome 10
proteins.blurb: Lipid phosphatase that switches off the PI3K→AKT growth signal.

proteins.name: Toll-like receptor 4
proteins.milestone: Human Toll homolog described (Medzhitov & Janeway); LPS sensor in 1998
proteins.blurb: Detects bacterial lipopolysaccharide and triggers inflammation.

proteins.name: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase parkin
proteins.milestone: Gene identified in autosomal recessive juvenile parkinsonism
proteins.blurb: Tags damaged mitochondria with ubiquitin so they can be recycled.

proteins.name: β-secretase 1
proteins.milestone: Identified as the β-secretase that starts amyloid-β production
proteins.blurb: Makes the first cut in APP that leads to amyloid-β.

proteins.name: Angiotensin-converting enzyme 2
proteins.milestone: Discovered as a homolog of ACE; later the entry receptor for SARS-CoV (2003) and SARS-CoV-2 (2020)
proteins.blurb: Counterbalances ACE; also the door SARS-CoV-2 uses to enter cells.

proteins.name: Serine protease HTRA2 (Omi)
proteins.milestone: Found to be released from mitochondria to promote apoptosis
proteins.blurb: Mitochondrial protease that, when released, removes the brakes on caspases.

proteins.name: Prestin
proteins.milestone: Identified as the outer-hair-cell motor (Zheng et al.)
proteins.blurb: Membrane motor that lengthens and shortens hair cells to amplify sound.

proteins.name: Endoribonuclease Dicer
proteins.milestone: Identified as the enzyme that makes small RNAs (Bernstein et al.)
proteins.blurb: Chops double-stranded RNA into microRNAs and siRNAs for gene silencing.

proteins.name: Forkhead box protein P3
proteins.milestone: Mutations found to cause IPEX syndrome
proteins.blurb: Defines regulatory T cells that stop the immune system attacking the body.

proteins.name: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin 9
proteins.milestone: Mutations found to cause familial hypercholesterolemia
proteins.blurb: Escorts the LDL receptor to destruction, raising blood cholesterol.

proteins.name: Serine/threonine-protein kinase PINK1
proteins.milestone: Mutations linked to early-onset Parkinson's disease
proteins.blurb: Flags damaged mitochondria so Parkin can mark them for disposal (mitophagy).

proteins.name: Mitochondrial antiviral-signaling protein
proteins.milestone: Identified on mitochondria (Seth, Sun, Ea & Chen)
proteins.blurb: Forms signalling filaments on mitochondria when viral RNA is sensed.

proteins.name: Stimulator of interferon genes protein
proteins.milestone: Discovered as an ER innate-immune adaptor (Ishikawa & Barber)
proteins.blurb: Receives cGAMP on the ER and launches the interferon response.

proteins.name: Cyclic GMP-AMP synthase
proteins.milestone: Discovered as the cytosolic DNA sensor (Sun, Wu, Chen et al.)
proteins.blurb: Detects DNA where it shouldn't be (the cytosol) and makes the alarm molecule cGAMP.
